source: Ellamil, Dobson, Beeman & Christoff (2012) Evaluative and generative modes of thought during the creative process
finding: fMRI study where people designed book-cover illustrations on a drawing tablet and alternated between generating and evaluating. Generation preferentially recruited medial temporal lobe. Evaluation recruited executive and default regions together, plus rostrolateral PFC, insula and temporopolar cortex. Executive and default regions stayed positively connected throughout.
numbers: Abstract only read this session; sample size and statistics not verified (full text paywalled, no open copy found).
limits: Phases were self-switched, so generation and evaluation can overlap in time. One study, small fMRI sample, one task (drawing). Evaluation here is mixed analytic plus affective, not a cold critic.
agent_relevance: Supports separate passes for producing and judging, but says evaluation is not purely analytic: it uses affective and default-network processing. A code check is not the same operation as human evaluation.

source: Gonen-Yaacovi et al. (2013) Rostral and caudal prefrontal contribution to creativity: a meta-analysis of functional imaging data
finding: ALE meta-analysis of 34 imaging studies. Tasks that combine remote information activated more anterior lateral PFC than tasks of free generation of unusual responses. Both shared caudal PFC. Rostral PFC combines ideas, caudal PFC supports free generation.
numbers: 34 studies; shared left-hemisphere network (caudal lateral PFC, medial and lateral rostral PFC, inferior parietal, posterior temporal).
limits: Nearly all included studies are generation tasks. Almost none separate evaluation, so it says little about judging.
agent_relevance: Different creative operations (combine versus free-generate) use different machinery. Argues for naming the operation in each call, not one generic 'be creative' prompt.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Silvia & Schacter (2016) Creative cognition and brain network dynamics
finding: Across divergent thinking, poetry and music improvisation, the default and executive control networks, usually antagonistic, cooperate during creative thought. This is the main rival to a strict two-system split.
numbers: Abstract read only.
limits: Cooperation is shown for generation tasks; it does not show that judging and producing cannot be separated in time.
agent_relevance: Rival view: creativity may need joint generate-and-control, so a pure split into generator and critic calls may lose something. Test it, do not assume.

source: Beaty et al. (2014) Creativity and the default network: a functional connectivity analysis of the creative brain at rest
finding: High-creative group showed stronger connectivity between left inferior frontal gyrus and the whole default network than the low-creative group.
numbers: Abstract read only. Group sizes not verified.
limits: Resting state, extreme-group design, no generation or evaluation phase.
agent_relevance: Individual differences point to cooperation between control and imaginative systems, not isolation of the two.

source: Jia & Zeng (2021) EEG signals respond differently to idea generation, idea evolution and evaluation in a loosely controlled creativity experiment
finding: Modified figural Torrance task with EEG. Alpha power fell from rest in all three modes. Task completion time differed across generation, evolution and evaluation.
numbers: Repeated-measures F(2,54)=69.0 for completion time (about 28 participants, from df).
limits: 'Evaluation' here meant rating the difficulty of thinking and drawing, not judging idea quality. It is not a clean test of idea evaluation.
agent_relevance: Papers labelled 'evaluation' often do not judge idea quality. Check what the task asked before using it as evidence for G5/G8.

source: Network oscillations imply the highest cognitive workload and lowest cognitive control during idea generation in open-ended creation tasks (2021, Sci Rep)
finding: EEG during design tasks. Idea generation showed the highest workload and the lowest cognitive control compared with problem understanding, idea evaluation and self-rating. Microstate class C (negatively tied to the control network) was most frequent in generation, and generation had the shortest temporal correlation times (looser network switching).
numbers: Task-related power in delta, theta, alpha and beta plus EEG microstate analysis; 42 participants appear in the text (exact analysed N not checked).
limits: Loosely controlled design task, phases defined by instruction, EEG has poor spatial resolution. Authors validated the setup only by comparison with the literature.
agent_relevance: Independent EEG evidence that producing ideas is low-control and judging is higher-control. Supports giving the two steps different instructions and temperatures.

source: Rominger et al. (2019) Creativity is associated with a characteristic U-shaped function of alpha power changes accompanied by an early increase in functional coupling
finding: EEG during alternate-uses ideation. More original ideas went with a faster early increase in task-related power; less original ideas showed relatively stronger increases at later stages. Creative ideation unfolds over stages.
numbers: 86 analysed participants (102 recruited); self-paced single best-idea task, 15 s maximum.
limits: Participants rated the originality of their own idea before speaking it, so self-evaluation is blended in. Effects are small.
agent_relevance: Ideation has early and late stages; the scaffold should not judge during the early stage.

source: Use a spoon as a spade? Changes in the upper and lower alpha bands in evaluating alternate object use (2018)
finding: When people judge whether a given use is common or uncommon, alternate uses cost more semantic work than common uses: more upper-alpha activity over parieto-occipital sites, more left anterior lower-alpha activity, and a larger N400 (400-500 ms) that extended into 500-1000 ms.
numbers: Word-pair evaluation task; sample size not extracted.
limits: Judging someone else's word pairs is not judging one's own idea.
agent_relevance: Judging a novel idea is itself costly re-representation work, so a judge call needs room and context. Judging is not free.

source: Towards a neural model of creative evaluation in advertising: an electrophysiological study (2020)
finding: ERP study judging ads that varied in novelty and usefulness. Novelty gave early N1-P2 effects, effort on novel content gave N200-500, and usefulness gave a late positive component. Authors propose three sub-processes: novelty perception, conception expansion, value selection.
numbers: 31 subjects.
limits: Domain is advertising; stimuli were constructed. Model is proposed, not tested against alternatives.
agent_relevance: Evaluation has at least two checks: is it new, is it useful. A judge prompt could score these separately instead of one overall rating.

source: The human reward system encodes the subjective value of ideas during creative thinking (2025, Commun Biol)
finding: fMRI, 40 recruited, 38 analysed. Default network encoded originality, executive network encoded adequacy, and the reward (valuation) system, including vmPFC, encoded the subjective value of an idea. Behavioural result from an earlier study was replicated: valuation depends on both originality and adequacy and differs by person.
numbers: N=38 analysed; vmPFC peak (-8, 48, -10), t(37)=8.81.
limits: Word-association ideas are tiny. Replication of behaviour is by the same group.
agent_relevance: Evaluation splits into monitoring (originality, adequacy) and valuation (weighting them). The weight is a personal preference, so the agent should set the originality-versus-adequacy weight explicitly in code.

source: Functional lateralization of the medial temporal lobe in novel associative processing during creativity evaluation (2023)
finding: When people evaluated novel designs, right MTL responded to novelty and left MTL to usefulness. Left parahippocampal patterns predicted later judgments of 'truly creative'. So the medial temporal lobe is involved in evaluation too, which complicates the reading that MTL belongs only to generation.
numbers: Small fMRI sample (not extracted).
limits: Constructed design stimuli. Challenges the clean 'MTL = generation' reading of Ellamil et al.
agent_relevance: A caution against building a strict brain-region story into the schema. Use only the behavioural findings.

source: Heinonen et al. (2016) Default mode and executive networks areas: association with the serial order in divergent thinking
finding: With 16 participants silently generating alternative uses, left anterior insula was active versus object identification. Activation in anterior cingulate rose with the serial order of the idea.
numbers: n=16. Abstract read only.
limits: Small n; silent generation, so timing of ideas is inferred.
agent_relevance: Later ideas need more control, which fits a long generate pass before any judging.

source: Meta-analysis of fMRI studies of divergent thinking using activation likelihood estimation (2020)
finding: 20 studies met criteria. Four clusters: left inferior parietal, left inferior frontal and precentral, superior and medial frontal, right cerebellum. Mostly semantic network regions, not clearly the default-network story.
numbers: 19 experiments, 162 foci, 596 participants.
limits: All divergent-thinking generation tasks. Says nothing on evaluation.
agent_relevance: The fMRI base for 'generation' is the semantic retrieval network. Generation quality may be about retrieval breadth, which sampling can supply.

source: Beaty et al. (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity
finding: Connectome-based prediction of creative ability involved default, executive and salience networks together; cited as evidence for network cooperation rather than separation.
numbers: Not opened beyond the search listing.
limits: Correlational; individual traits, not within-task phases.
agent_relevance: Weak support only. Do not cite for numbers.

source: Dynamic switching between brain networks predicts creative ability (2025)
finding: Largest creativity neuroscience sample so far: N=2433 across 10 samples (Austria, Canada, China, Japan, US). Creative ability followed an inverted U with the balance of default-executive switching. Task-fMRI validation (N=31) showed higher switching during idea generation than control and replicated the inverted U.
numbers: Correlation between the two constructs differed by site: r=0.32, 0.33, 0.39 in three datasets, but 0.07 and 0.13 (CIs include 0) in two others.
limits: Resting-state measures; effect not uniform across samples; validation sample small.
agent_relevance: Best current large-sample result. Both too little and too much coupling hurt. Pure isolation of generator and judge is not what good creators show; the best coupling is intermediate.

source: Si, Yang & Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas? A large-scale human study with 100+ NLP researchers
finding: Blind review by 79 experts of 49 ideas per condition. Novelty (1-10): human 4.84, AI 5.64, AI plus human rerank 5.81. AI ideas rated significantly more novel (p<0.05); feasibility slightly lower. Pipeline is over-generate then rank.
numbers: 79 reviewers, 49 idea writers, 49 ideas per condition, 7 NLP topics; Welch t-tests with Bonferroni correction.
limits: Idea-stage ratings only, no execution. 24 of 79 reviewers also wrote ideas. Human writers may not have submitted their best ideas.
agent_relevance: The generate-many then select design can beat expert-written novelty. But see the selector result below.

source: Si, Yang & Hashimoto (2024) section 7.2: LLMs cannot evaluate ideas reliably
finding: LLM judges cannot rank ideas. Against average expert score (top vs bottom 25%, balanced accuracy): human inter-reviewer agreement 56.1%; GPT-4o direct 50.0%; GPT-4o pairwise 45.0%; Claude-3.5 direct 51.7%; Claude-3.5 pairwise 53.3%; AI Scientist reviewer 43.3%. Chance is 50%.
numbers: Reference points: NeurIPS 2021 reviewer consistency 66.0%, ICLR 2024 71.9%. On ICLR accepted/rejected pairs Claude-3.5 reached 71.4%, GPT-4o 61.1%, Claude-3-Opus 63.5%.
limits: Metric is noisy with 49 ideas per condition. Human agreement is also low on unexecuted ideas.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for G8: a model judge of idea novelty or quality is near chance. Pairwise comparison is the best LLM judge but no better than humans disagreeing.

source: Si, Yang & Hashimoto (2024) section 7.1: LLMs lack diversity in idea generation
finding: From 4000 generated seed ideas per topic, only 200 were non-duplicates (cosine similarity above 0.8 counted as duplicate). New batches kept repeating earlier ideas and accumulated unique ideas plateaued.
numbers: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, threshold 0.8, 4000 seeds per topic.
limits: One embedding model and one threshold; a limit of that agent's pipeline.
agent_relevance: Generation-side bottleneck. More samples from one model do not buy more distinct ideas, so selection cannot fix a weak pool. Add distinctness filtering in code.

source: Si, Hashimoto & Yang (2025) The ideation-execution gap: execution outcomes of LLM-generated versus human research ideas
finding: 43 experts each spent over 100 hours executing randomly assigned ideas. After execution, AI ideas lost 1.049 on novelty, 1.760 on excitement and 1.879 on effectiveness (1-10), while human ideas changed by -0.010, +0.078 and -0.052. Drops differed significantly (FDR p<0.05) on all four metrics. Ranking flipped: excitement 3.90 (AI) vs 4.48 (human); effectiveness 4.13 vs 4.78.
numbers: N=43 projects. The post-execution ranking flip itself was not significant. Spearman correlation of ideation and execution scores was weak (e.g. 0.077) and moderately negative for AI excitement.
limits: Small sample; recruited executors; one field (NLP prompting research).
agent_relevance: Judging ideas before running them is unreliable even for expert panels. G8 stands: settle novelty and value by running or checking, not opinion.

source: Huang et al. (2023, ICLR 2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
finding: Without outside feedback, asking the model to critique and fix its own answer made accuracy worse. GPT-3.5 CommonsenseQA fell from 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. With oracle labels, GPT-3.5 GSM8K rose 75.9 to 84.3 and HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0; GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 on GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA; also GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2.
limits: Reasoning tasks with checkable answers. Not about creative quality. Row labels in the table are assigned by me from column order.
agent_relevance: Same model judging its own output with no real signal makes it worse. Supports judging that uses outside signals only (G2, G5).

source: Panickssery, Bowman & Feng (2024) LLM evaluators recognize and favor their own generations
finding: Frontier models prefer their own text when judging summaries and can tell their text from others'. GPT-4 recognised itself with 73.5% accuracy out of the box. After fine-tuning on 500 examples GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 got over 90% self-recognition. Self-preference grew linearly with self-recognition.
numbers: News summarisation sets (CNN/DailyMail, XSUM); pairwise and individual scoring; GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama 2.
limits: Summaries, not ideas. Correlational plus a fine-tuning intervention for causation.
agent_relevance: A judge that wrote the text is biased. Use a different model or hide authorship (G5 already says the judge sees no authorship).

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
finding: GPT-4 judge agrees with humans above 80%, as much as humans agree with each other. Biases: position (most judges favor first position); verbosity (all judges fall for repeated-list padding on 23 answers, GPT-4 resists best); self-enhancement (GPT-4 +10% win rate for itself, Claude-v1 +25%, GPT-3.5 none). Poor at grading maths it can solve.
numbers: Self-enhancement could not be shown conclusively; authors say data was limited.
limits: Chat-quality tasks with clear human preference, not creativity.
agent_relevance: General judge biases to remove in code: swap order, normalise length, hide authorship.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: deliberate problem solving with large language models
finding: Separating thought generation from thought evaluation (value or vote prompts) with search. Game of 24 with GPT-4: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT self-consistency (k=100) 9.0%, ToT breadth 1 45%, ToT breadth 5 74%. Best of 100 CoT samples reached only 49%.
numbers: Game of 24; also creative writing and mini crosswords.
limits: The evaluator works because states are checkable, as in arithmetic. Not shown for open-ended ideas. Costs many more calls.
agent_relevance: Positive case for a separate evaluation call when the judge can use a rule. ToT beat best-of-k at equal visited nodes.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large language monkeys: scaling inference compute with repeated sampling
finding: Coverage (any sample correct) rises with number of samples. On SWE-bench Lite, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 solves 15.9% with one sample and 56% with 250 samples, above the single-sample state of the art of 43%. Without automatic verifiers, majority voting and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples.
numbers: Tasks with automatic verification (code, proofs) versus word problems and others.
limits: The gain needs a verifier. Without it the extra samples do not help.
agent_relevance: Generate-then-select pays only when the selector is reliable. For ideas without a checker, the bottleneck is selection, matching Si et al.

source: Cobbe et al. (2021) Training verifiers to solve math word problems
finding: Training a separate verifier to judge sampled solutions gives about the same gain as a 30x larger model, and verifiers scale better with more data. Dropout strongly helps both fine-tuning and verification.
numbers: GSM8K (8.5K problems), 100 samples per problem (test@100).
limits: Verifier trained on labelled right and wrong solutions; maths with one correct answer.
agent_relevance: Support for separate generator and judge when there is ground truth to train a judge on. Not applicable to open creative output.

source: Lightman et al. (2023) Let's verify step by step
finding: Step-level judging (process reward model) beat outcome-only judging. On a MATH subset with best of 1860: PRM 78.2%, outcome reward model 72.4%, majority voting 69.6%.
numbers: MATH test subset; PRM800K step labels.
limits: Trained judges with human step labels; maths only.
agent_relevance: A judge that checks each step against real labels beats one that judges the final text. Small steps and real signal help; a vague overall opinion does not.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: iterative refinement with self-feedback
finding: One model generates, gives specific actionable feedback and refines. Reports about 20% absolute average gain over one-step generation across seven tasks; up to 13% absolute on code with strong models; 8.7% absolute on code optimization with GPT-4. Quality rises with iterations.
numbers: Seven tasks; GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4. Feedback is task-specific and cites concrete phrases.
limits: Self-generated feedback; later work (Huang et al.) finds gains vanish on reasoning tasks without an oracle signal. Some outcomes scored by LLM or metric.
agent_relevance: Rival result. Self-feedback can help when specific and the task has a clear metric. Test on our tasks; do not assume either way.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: evaluating language models for human-like diversity
finding: 20 leading models produce far less diversity than human writers; many produce fewer than 3 distinct responses in 10 queries. Larger models in a family are often less diverse than smaller ones. In-context regeneration (showing the model its earlier outputs) lifted diversity to roughly human writers; paraphrasing and 'be creative' system prompts were only marginally effective.
numbers: NB-Curated and NB-WildChat; distinct_k via clustered equivalence classes; quality via a reward model; human baseline is 8 paper authors; regeneration test on 100 prompts, 8 generations, three models.
limits: Human baseline is only 8 authors. Equivalence classifier is a learned model.
agent_relevance: Generation needs context on what is already made, enforced by code. 'Be more creative' wording does not help. Links to the pool problem in Si et al.

source: Gap note for this angle (no source)
finding: No study found that directly compares one-call generate-and-judge against separate-call generate-then-judge on creative quality at equal tokens. Closest are Tree of Thoughts (checkable tasks) and Si et al. (human-judged ideas, over-generate-and-rank).
numbers: Web search budget was exhausted; OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv listing endpoints were rate limited. Human idea-selection studies (Rietzschel, Nijstad and Stroebe; Girotra, Terwiesch and Ulrich) were not opened.
limits: A gap in this file, not evidence of absence.
agent_relevance: The planned NoveltyBench A/B test (SUBFIELDS item 1) fills a real gap; run it.
